mainTopic: Gifts from a גוי's produce (bought or deposited): must they be given to the כהן? Also, when the כהן acquires the lamb that redeems a פטר חמור
overview: This amud opens with the end of רבי חנינא's ruling: grain bought from a גוי after it was smoothed into piles (ממורחין) must be tithed, but the buyer keeps the gifts. The גמרא explains that a Jew must have done the מירוח while the grain still belonged to the גוי. The buyer must tithe because a גוי cannot cancel the holiness of ארץ ישראל. He keeps the gifts because he stands in the place of the גוי, whom the כהן could never sue. Next the גמרא quotes a משנה in דמאי about produce deposited with a גוי, where the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון disagree. רבי אלעזר explains that everyone agrees the gifts must be separated, and they argue only about giving them to the כהן. אביי challenges this from רבי חנינא's ruling. רב דימי answers that the משנה speaks of תרומה גדולה while רבי חנינא speaks of תרומת מעשר, and אביי supports this with a פסוק taught by רבי יהושע בן לוי. Finally the גמרא returns to our משנה and teaches that the lamb used to redeem a פטר חמור belongs to the כהן from the moment it is separated.

steps.title: Smoothed grain bought from a גוי: tithe it, but keep the gifts
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא's ruling, quoted by רבי שמואל, says that smoothed piles of grain bought from a גוי must be tithed, but the gifts stay with the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the grain was already smoothed into piles when bought from the גוי, the buyer separates the מעשרות, but they remain his.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the end of רבי חנינא's ruling (quoted by רבי שמואל) about buying grain from a גוי. If the grain was already smoothed into piles (ממורחין), the buyer must separate the tithes, but he may keep them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מירוח, smoothing the grain pile, is the final processing step that makes grain obligated in תרומה and מעשר. The ruling has two halves. First, the obligation exists (מעשרן). Second, the buyer does not have to hand the gifts to a כהן or לוי (והן שלו). The next steps explain each half.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain smoothed into a finished pile, the stage that triggers the tithing obligation
He must separate the tithes from them

steps.confusionAlert: 'והן שלו' does not mean the grain is exempt. He still has to separate the tithes. He just does not have to give them away.

phrases.english: If they were already smoothed when bought from the non-Jew,
phrases.notes: מירוח is the act that completes processing and creates the obligation of tithes.

phrases.english: he tithes them, but they are his.
phrases.notes: He separates the gifts but keeps them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְמוֹרָחִין מִן הַגּוֹי מְעַשְּׂרָן וְהֵן שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי חנינא's statement (quoted by רבי שמואל) that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grain bought from a גוי after מירוח must be tithed, but the buyer keeps the gifts.

steps.title: Who smoothed the grain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who did the מירוח in the case of רבי חנינא's ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: who smoothed the grain, the גוי or a Jew? This sets up the next two moves, which test each possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since מירוח is the moment the obligation begins, it matters who did it. The identity of the person doing the מירוח decides whether there is any obligation at all.

phrases.english: Who smoothed them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact case behind the ruling in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the מירוח was done by the גוי or by a Jew.

steps.title: It cannot be that the גוי smoothed it
steps.stepSummary: If the גוי did the מירוח, the grain would be fully exempt, because the פסוק says 'your grain' and not a גוי's grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the גוי smoothed them, the תורה says 'your grain', not the grain of a גוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possibility, that the גוי did the smoothing, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'דגנך' teaches that grain whose מירוח was done by a גוי is not obligated. If the גוי did the מירוח, there would be no obligation at all, so the ruling could not say מעשרן. This option must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a possibility about to be rejected)
'Your grain', the Torah's wording for tithes
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: If you say that a non-Jew smoothed them —
the Torah said 'your grain',
and not the grain of a non-Jew!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and eliminates the first answer to the question in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the ברייתא as a case where the גוי did the מירוח.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Grain smoothed by a גוי is exempt under 'דגנך', so 'מעשרן' could not apply.

steps.title: A Jew smoothed it while the גוי still owned it
steps.stepSummary: The case is that a Jew did the מירוח while the grain was still in the גוי's ownership, before he bought it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a Jew smoothed them while they were still in the גוי's possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct case: a Jew smoothed the grain, but it still belonged to the גוי at that time. This sets up the explanation of both halves of the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is in between. A Jew's action finished the grain, so 'דגנך' does not rule it out. But the owner at the moment of מירוח was a גוי. That mix explains why there is an obligation, yet a weaker one with respect to giving the gifts away.

phrases.english: Rather, a Jew smoothed them
while in the non-Jew's possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after step 3 rejected the first possibility.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A Jew did the מירוח while the grain still belonged to the גוי.

steps.title: Why the grain must be tithed
steps.stepSummary: Tithing is required because a גוי's ownership of land in ארץ ישראל cannot remove the produce from the obligation of מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He must tithe them, because a גוי has no ownership in ארץ ישראל strong enough to cancel the obligation of מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of the ruling, מעשרן. The grain stays obligated even though a גוי owned it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'אין קנין לגוי בארץ ישראל להפקיע ממעשר' means a גוי's ownership does not remove the land's holiness. The produce therefore keeps its obligation. Since a Jew did the מירוח, the obligation takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew's acquisition does not have full power

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle 'אין קנין לגוי בארץ ישראל להפקיע ממעשר' is a major principle across ש״ס, and other sources argue about it.

phrases.english: He tithes them,
because a non-Jew has no acquisition in the Land of Israel
to remove it from the obligation of tithe,

steps.triggerLanguage: מְעַשְּׂרָן דְּאֵין קִנְיָן לְגוֹי בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of the ruling using the case set up in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The obligation stands because a גוי's ownership cannot cancel the land's holiness.

steps.title: Why the buyer keeps the tithes
steps.stepSummary: The buyer keeps the gifts because he can tell the כהן that he stands in the place of the גוי, whom the כהן could never sue.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they are his, because he can say to the כהן: 'I come on the strength of a man you could not take to court.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of the ruling, והן שלו. The buyer separates the gifts but does not have to give them away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer acquired the grain from the גוי, so he holds the גוי's rights. The כהן had no claim against the גוי for the gifts. So he has no claim against the buyer either. The buyer must separate the gifts, but nobody can force him to hand them over.

keyTerms.meaning: I come on the strength of (stand in someone's legal place)

steps.whatToRemember: Grain bought from a גוי after a Jew did the מירוח has two results. It must be tithed (אין קנין לגוי להפקיע). But the buyer keeps the gifts (קאתינא מכח גברא).

phrases.english: And they are his —
because he says to him (the priest): I come
on the strength of a man
with whom you could not engage
phrases.notes: The bracketed word is the corrected reading.

phrases.english: in a lawsuit.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָאָתֵינָא מִכֹּחַ גַּבְרָא דְּלָא מָצֵית אִישְׁתַּעוֹיֵי דִּינָא בַּהֲדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation by addressing the second half of the ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The buyer inherits the גוי's legal position, and the כהן has no claim against that position.

steps.title: New source: produce deposited with a כותי or an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in דמאי: produce deposited with a כותי or an עם הארץ keeps its original status regarding מעשר and שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: one who deposits his produce with a כותי or with an עם הארץ, it stays in its original status regarding מעשר and שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion by quoting a משנה from מסכת דמאי. This sets up an analysis that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that we do not suspect the כותי or the עם הארץ of swapping the deposited produce for untithed produce or for produce of שביעית. The produce keeps its original חזקה. The discussion that follows (steps 8–12) focuses on the next case in this משנה, a deposit with a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
An unlearned Jew, not trusted about tithes

steps.confusionAlert: 'בחזקתן' means the produce stays as it was when deposited. It does not mean it becomes doubtful or needs re-tithing.

phrases.english: We learned there:
One who deposits his produce with a Samaritan
or with an unlearned Jew,
they stay in their presumed status regarding tithe and the Sabbatical Year.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם הַמַּפְקִיד פֵּירוֹתָיו אֵצֶל הַכּוּתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related source. Its גוי clause will lead back to the same question as steps 1–6: whether gifts from a גוי's produce must be given to the כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce deposited with a כותי or an עם הארץ keeps its original status for מעשר and שביעית.

steps.title: Produce deposited with a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in דמאי ends with the case of produce left with a גוי. The תנא קמא says it is treated like the גוי's own produce. רבי שמעון says it is treated as דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone left his produce with a גוי, it is treated like the גוי's produce. רבי שמעון says it is treated as דמאי (doubtfully tithed).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה it started in the last step. It now gives the last case: produce left with a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the גוי may have swapped the owner's produce for his own. The תנא קמא assumes he did swap it, so the produce counts as the גוי's. רבי שמעון says we only have a doubt, so the produce has the status of דמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Like his produce, meaning treated like the גוי's own produce
Produce that may or may not have been tithed

phrases.english: [If deposited] with a gentile, it is like his (the gentile's) produce,
phrases.notes: We assume the gentile swapped it for his own produce.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: it is demai (doubtful).
phrases.notes: It is only a doubt whether he swapped it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה quoted in step 7, now giving the case of a גוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce deposited with a גוי: the תנא קמא treats it as the גוי's produce, and רבי שמעון treats it as דמאי.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר explains what the argument is about
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says everyone agrees the gifts must be separated. The only argument is whether they must be given to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: about separating the gifts, everyone agrees. They only argue about giving them to the כהן. The תנא קמא holds the גוי certainly swapped the produce, so the owner must give the gifts to the כהן. רבי שמעון holds it is only a doubt (דמאי).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר narrows down the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון. Both say you must separate the gifts. They only disagree about handing them over to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, the swap is certain, so the owner definitely owes the gifts and must give them away. According to רבי שמעון, it is only a doubt. With a doubt, the כהן cannot demand the gifts, since whoever wants to take money from another must bring proof. So the owner separates the gifts but does not have to hand them over.

keyTerms.meaning: To separate (set aside) the gifts from the produce
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון lets you skip separating the gifts. Everyone agrees they must be separated. The argument is only about giving them to the כהן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Regarding separating [the gifts], everyone agrees;
where they argue is about giving them to the priest.
The first tanna holds: he certainly swapped them,
and so he must give them to the priest;
and Rabbi Shimon holds: it is demai.
phrases.notes: Because it is a doubt, the כהן cannot demand the gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְהַפְרִישׁ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains exactly what the argument in step 8 is about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All agree the gifts must be separated. The argument is only over giving them to the כהן: the תנא קמא says the swap is certain, so they must be given, and רבי שמעון says it is a doubt, so they need not be given.

steps.title: אביי challenges from רבי חנינא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that רבי אלעזר's explanation implies something. If the swap were certain, everyone would require giving to the כהן. But רבי חנינא ruled that someone who buys processed טבל from a גוי tithes it and keeps the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי sat and taught this teaching. אביי said to him: the only reason רבי שמעון disagrees is that we are unsure whether the גוי swapped the produce. That means if he definitely swapped it, everyone would say the gifts must go to the כהן. But didn't רבי שמואל say in the name of רבי חנינא: someone who buys טבל from a גוי after it was smoothed into piles tithes it, and the gifts belong to him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי teaches רבי אלעזר's explanation. אביי attacks it using רבי חנינא's ruling, the same one we saw earlier about the buyer keeping the gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גוי swapped the produce, the owner is getting back the גוי's טבל. That is just like buying טבל from a גוי. רבי חנינא ruled that such a buyer separates the gifts but keeps them. So how could the תנא קמא require giving them to the כהן?

keyTerms.meaning: טבל: produce from which the gifts have not yet been separated
Smoothed into piles (מירוח), the processing step that creates the obligation to tithe
And they (the gifts) are his to keep

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the deposit case back to the main sugya. It is the same buyer-keeps-the-gifts rule explained in step 6.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב דִּימִי וְקָאָמַר לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Dimi sat and stated this teaching;
Abaye said to him:
The reason is that we are in doubt
whether he swapped them or did not swap them;
but if he certainly swapped them,
everyone agrees he must give them to the priest.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Shmuel say in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
One who buys untithed produce from a gentile already smoothed into piles
tithes them, and they (the gifts) are his!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from רבי אלעזר's explanation in step 9 and shows it clashes with רבי חנינא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that, if the swap is certain, the gifts must be given to the כהן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A certain swap makes this the same as buying טבל from a גוי. In that case רבי חנינא rules that the buyer keeps the gifts.

steps.title: The two rulings speak about different gifts
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the two rulings deal with different gifts. The משנה, which requires giving, is about תרומה גדולה. רבי חנינא's ruling, which lets the buyer keep the gift, is about תרומת מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps here (the משנה) it is talking about תרומה גדולה, and there (רבי חנינא) it is talking about תרומת מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers אביי. He says the two rulings do not contradict each other because each one is about a different gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The requirement to give to the כהן applies to תרומה גדולה, the first gift taken from the crop. The rule that 'the gifts are his' applies to תרומת מעשר, the gift taken out of the tithe. With this split, the contradiction disappears. The text here is a suggestion ('perhaps'), not a firm conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: The main תרומה, separated first from the crop and given to a כהן
The tenth of the מעשר that the לוי separates and gives to a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: Deposit with a גוי: everyone agrees the gifts must be separated. The question is giving them away. The apparent conflict with רבי חנינא is resolved by splitting תרומה גדולה (must be given) from תרומת מעשר (the buyer may keep it).

phrases.english: Perhaps here it refers to teruma gedola,
phrases.notes: Here = the משנה, which requires giving to the כהן.

phrases.english: there it refers to teruma of the tithe!
phrases.notes: There = רבי חנינא's ruling, that the buyer keeps it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא כָּאן בִּתְרוּמָה גְּדוֹלָה כָּאן בִּתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (כאן... כאן): each ruling applies to a different type of gift.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings seemed to be about the same gifts, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The duty to give to the כהן is about תרומה גדולה, while רבי חנינא's 'they are his' is about תרומת מעשר.

steps.title: A verse shows that תרומת מעשר from a גוי's produce is not given to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: אביי recalls that רבי יהושע בן לוי learned from a פסוק that someone who buys processed טבל from a גוי does not give the תרומת מעשר to the כהן. This supports the answer in step 11.
steps.simpleTranslation: You reminded me of something רבי יהושע בן לוי said. How do we know that someone who buys processed טבל from a גוי is exempt from תרומת מעשר? The פסוק says: 'Speak to the לויים and tell them: when you take from בני ישראל.' This teaches that טבל you buy from a Jew requires you to separate תרומת מעשר and give it to the כהן. טבל you buy from a גוי does not require you to separate תרומת מעשר and give it to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי says, 'You reminded me,' and quotes a teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי. That teaching gives a source from the תורה for the idea in step 11 that תרומת מעשר from a גוי's produce stays with the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about תרומת מעשר says 'when you take from בני ישראל.' The word 'בני ישראל' limits the rule of giving תרומת מעשר to the כהן to produce that came from a Jew. Produce bought from a גוי is left out, which explains why רבי חנינא let the buyer keep the gift.

keyTerms.meaning: You reminded me of a teaching
Produce from which the required gifts have not yet been taken
Smoothed into piles, meaning fully processed so the obligation to tithe has started
The tenth of the לוי's tithe, which is given to a כהן
From where do we learn it?

steps.confusionAlert: Read the end of the teaching together: 'you do not separate it AND give it to the כהן.' In this sugya the main point is that the gift is not given to the כהן. That matches רבי חנינא's ruling in step 10 that the buyer tithes and keeps the gift.
steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms the answer in step 11. רבי חנינא's ruling deals only with תרומת מעשר, and that ruling has a clear source in a פסוק.

phrases.english: You reminded me of a teaching
phrases.notes: Said by אביי (named in the Sefaria translation).

phrases.english: that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לַלּוֹקֵחַ טְבָלִים מְמוֹרָחִין מִן הַגּוֹי
phrases.english: From where do we know that one who buys smoothed untithed produce from a gentile
is exempt from the teruma of the tithe?
As it is stated: "And to the Levites you shall speak
and you shall say to them:
When you take from the children of Israel"
phrases.notes: The key words are 'from the children of Israel.'

phrases.english: Untithed produce that you buy from Jews:
you separate the teruma of the tithe from it
and give it to the priest;
untithed produce that you buy from a gentile:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה מַפְרִישׁ מֵהֶן תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר
phrases.english: you do not separate the teruma of the tithe from it
and give it to the priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַזְכַּרְתַּן מִילְּתָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source from a פסוק that supports the answer in step 11 about תרומת מעשר.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי חנינא's ruling, that the buyer keeps the gift, applies to תרומת מעשר from טבל bought from a גוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading of 'כי תקחו מאת בני ישראל' (במדבר יח:כו).

steps.title: Back to the משנה: where did the lamb die?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to our משנה's rule that one may benefit from the redemption lamb if it dies. It asks where the lamb died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And if it dies, one may benefit from it.' Where did it die?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to our משנה, which discusses the lamb used to redeem a פטר חמור. It asks where the lamb died, and this question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say whose house the lamb was in when it died. The גמרא needs to know this to understand what new point the משנה is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: One may benefit from it, because it is not sacred property

phrases.english: "And if it dies, one may derive benefit from it."
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה about the lamb that redeems a פטר חמור.

phrases.english: Where did it die?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם מֵת נֶהֱנִים בּוֹ. דְּמִית הֵיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about produce from a גוי and returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what situation does the משנה's rule apply: did the lamb die with the כהן or with the owner?

steps.title: Either case seems too obvious to need teaching
steps.stepSummary: If the lamb died in the כהן's house, it obviously belongs to him. If it died in the owner's house, it is still obvious. So why does the משנה need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it died in the כהן's house and the כהן benefits from it, that is obvious, because it is his property. Rather, say it died in the owner's house and the כהן benefits from it. That is also obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries both possible answers to its question. It finds that each one seems too obvious for the משנה to bother teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the כהן's house, the lamb is clearly his own non-sacred property. The גמרא also says that the case of the owner's house seems obvious. That leaves the משנה with no new point, which is the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why teach it?
The owner, the Jew who redeemed the donkey

phrases.english: If we say that it died in the priest's house,
and the priest benefits from it,
it is obvious, it is his property!
Rather, say that it died in the owner's house
and the priest benefits from it,
this too is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests both possible answers to the question in step 13 and finds each one obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משנה's statement 'ואם מת נהנים בו.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In both possible cases the result is obvious, so the משנה seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: The lamb belongs to the כהן from the moment it is separated
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought the כהן owns the lamb only once he receives it. The משנה teaches that it belongs to him as soon as the owner separates it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that as long as the lamb has not reached the כהן's hands, he has not acquired it. So the משנה teaches us that from the moment the owner separated it, it is in the כהן's possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case of the owner's house is not obvious after all. The משנה teaches when the כהן becomes the owner of the lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person might assume a gift belongs to the כהן only after he takes it into his hands. The משנה teaches that separating the lamb is enough to make it the כהן's property. So even if it dies while still in the owner's house, it is the כהן's lamb and he may benefit from it.
steps.whatToRemember: The lamb that redeems a פטר חמור becomes the כהן's property the moment it is separated, not only when he receives it. That is why he may benefit from it even if it dies in the owner's house.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that, for this gift, separating it is enough to transfer ownership to the כהן, even before he physically takes it.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say
that as long as it has not reached his hand
he has not acquired it;
therefore it teaches us
that from the time he separated it
it stands in the priest's possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by showing that the case of the owner's house is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the case is not obvious by naming a mistaken assumption the משנה comes to correct.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן acquires the lamb only once it reaches his hands.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lamb belongs to the כהן from the moment it is separated.
